officialTitle: Nivolumab plus Ipilimumab in Advanced Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer

primaryEndpoints: OS with nivolumab plus ipilimumab vs chemotherapy (PD-L1 ≥1%)
design.notes: PD-L1 ≥1%: 1:1:1 to nivolumab-ipilimumab, nivolumab, or chemotherapy. PD-L1 <1%: 1:1:1 to nivolumab-ipilimumab, nivolumab-chemotherapy, or chemotherapy. Only the OS primary endpoint reported in this publication is curated.

clinicalQuestion: Does first-line dual checkpoint blockade with nivolumab plus ipilimumab improve overall survival over chemotherapy in advanced NSCLC?

pico.population: Stage IV or recurrent NSCLC, no previous chemotherapy, stratified into PD-L1 ≥1% and <1% cohorts
pico.comparator: Platinum-doublet chemotherapy (additional arms: nivolumab alone; nivolumab plus chemotherapy)
pico.outcomes: Primary (this report): OS with nivolumab plus ipilimumab vs chemotherapy in PD-L1 ≥1%

publications.title: Nivolumab plus Ipilimumab in Advanced Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer.
publications.label: Part 1 OS analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: Among the patients with a PD-L1 expression level of 1% or more, the median duration of overall survival was 17.1 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 15.0 to 20.1) with nivolumab plus ipilimumab and 14.9 months (95% CI, 12.7 to 16.7) with chemotherapy (P = 0.007), with 2-year overall survival rates of 40.0% and 32.8%, respectively.

The overall survival benefit was also observed in patients with a PD-L1 expression level of less than 1%, with a median duration of 17.2 months (95% CI, 12.8 to 22.0) with nivolumab plus ipilimumab and 12.2 months (95% CI, 9.2 to 14.3) with chemotherapy.

Among all the patients in the trial, the median duration of overall survival was 17.1 months (95% CI, 15.2 to 19.9) with nivolumab plus ipilimumab and 13.9 months (95% CI, 12.2 to 15.1) with chemotherapy.
The median duration of response was 23.2 months with nivolumab plus ipilimumab and 6.2 months with chemotherapy.

safety.description: Grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events (overall population)
safety.sourceQuote: The percentage of patients with grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events in the overall population was 32.8% with nivolumab plus ipilimumab and 36.0% with chemotherapy.

strengths: Large randomised phase III with PD-L1-stratified cohorts

clinicalImplications.text: Established nivolumab plus ipilimumab as a chemotherapy-free first-line option for advanced NSCLC without targetable drivers, including PD-L1-negative tumours.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Dual checkpoint blockade is one option where PD-L1 is <1%, a group in which PD-1 monotherapy is not used.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 31562796. Earlier TMB-based PFS report and later long-term updates not ingested. Doses not printed in abstract.
